subject: ThermaLiQ POC — conditional pricing waiver & packaging restructure request
messages:
From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: priyom_das@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-12T09:23:00-07:00
Subject: Thermaliq POC — conditional pricing waiver & packaging restructure request

Team —

Quick summary: ThermaliQ is asking for a one-off commercial structure to land a 6-month POC that converts to a 12-month commitment. They want a 35% blended discount off list for year one, plus a packaging change to include reserved capacity (Dedicated) for predictable latency. They signalled procurement would only move forward with both items in place.

Why this matters: ThermaliQ is a strategic target in the cardio imaging vertical; if we win the POC it’s a clear path to a multi-region deployment and an enterprise license opportunity (~$600k ARR run-rate in year 2). But the requested economics are outside current guardrails.

My proposal (recommended concession):
- Pilot term: 6 months, prepaid at 50% of pilot commitment up front.
- Discount: 20% off list for the first 12 months (applied to all token/seat usage up to agreed committed usage).
- Packaging: enable Dedicated pool with a capped burst allowance (10% over commit) — Dedicated adds $X/mo baseline (see attached spreadsheet for cost model).
- On conversion to 12-month contract: step-down pricing to standard tiered list, with a one-time onboarding credit equal to 10% of pilot spend.

Financial trade-offs: with the 20% concession and Dedicated baseline, expected first-year Gross Margin impact is ~14% vs. baseline; upside on conversion is material. The attached 'thermaliq_proposal_v2.xlsx' includes sensitivity tables (commits of 25k/50k/100k tokens/day) and an estimated CAC-to-LTV ratio.

Ask: I need VP/CFO-level sign-off to approve the 20% one-off concession and the Dedicated packaging exception (this is outside published packaging options). Markus — can you review the attached and advise if you can sign off or whether we should push back to 15% + accelerated conversion incentives?

I’ve looped in Priyom for commercial approval language and Marissa for renewal/ops considerations.

Thanks,
Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Account Exec, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Thermaliq POC — conditional pricing waiver & packaging restructure request

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear write-up. A couple of notes:
- Confirmed revenue ops can instrument a consumption guardrail to prevent runaway usage during pilot. That mitigates risk.
- From a commercial playbook perspective, 20% is borderline but defendable if we get the conversion clause tied to committed MRR and a 12-month minimum.
- Please add expected onboarding dates and acceptance criteria to the SOW so we can tie the credit trigger to successful acceptance tests.

I’ll draft the commercial language and a quick canary clause that reduces the discount to 15% if conversion isn't executed by month 7. If Markus is comfortable with 20% we should attach a short exec memo for his signature.

Best,
Priyom

Priyom Das
Director, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-13T08:41:00-07:00
Subject: Exec memo: ThermaliQ pilot concession request (recommend approval)

Markus —

I reviewed Karthik's model and Priyom's proposed guardrails. I support approving a 20% first-year concession with the following absolute conditions:
1) Signed SOW with explicit acceptance criteria within 45 days of pilot start.
2) 50% pilot prepayment and non-refundable onboarding fee of $10k to cover Dedicated baseline provisioning.
3) Conversion triggers that revert pricing to list if conversion doesn't happen by day 210 (month 7) — per Priyom's canary clause (discount drops to 15% and onboarding credit is void).
4) Revenue ops to implement strict usage thresholds and daily alerts.

Rationale: With the prepayment + onboarding fee + tight acceptance criteria, the incremental risk is manageable and the probability of conversion (based on their exec signals and reference checks) is high. The upside over the next 18 months justifies a temporary concession to capture the enterprise footprint.

Recommendation for sign-off: Approve 20% one-off concession + Dedicated packaging exception with the four conditions above. If you prefer a more conservative approach, approve 15% with an automatic conversion bonus (3% rebate) if they sign within 90 days of pilot completion.

I’ve attached a one-page memo fragment that we can use for the official sign-off.

Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
VP, Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, priyom_das@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-14T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Exec memo: ThermaliQ pilot concession request (recommend approval)

Thanks all — reviewed the numbers and attachments. Decision: APPROVED with conditions.

Approved items:
- 20% discount for first 12 months during pilot and conversion (as outlined).
- Dedicated packaging exception (reserve pool + 10% burst) for pilot only.

Conditions (must be enforced before signature):
1) 50% pilot prepayment collected and onboarding fee processed to Production Finance.
2) Signed SOW with acceptance criteria and a conversion milestone tied to net-new committed usage.
3) Risk clause: if conversion is not signed by day 210, discount auto-reverts to 0% and we invoice any consumption above agreed committed usage at list rates retroactively (per terms in SOW).
4) Revenue Ops to set hard caps and daily alerting; Legal to add the billing true-up language.

Please prepare the formal exec sign-off memo (one-paragraph approval + conditions) that I can sign electronically. Also add a summary line item to the forecast and signal RevOps to create the charge schedule.

Markus
